topics.topic: Fixed endpoints and protocols for the service API and owner interface
questions: What exact listener endpoint and protocol does the release fix for the service API and for the owner interface?
What exact network address, port or socket does the release fix for the service API and for the owner interface, and where is HTTPS terminated?
What exact transport, host/interface and port or socket path does the release fix for the service API and for the owner interface?

quotes: the listener of each surface opened at the address the release fixes — the configuration names none (rule 1) — one that cannot be opened failing the start and closing those already opened.
judgement.why: Exact listener endpoints and protocols are release and public-contract details rather than State 2 behavioural rules.

topics.topic: Listener opening order and precedence of opening-failure diagnostics
questions: In what order are the service-API and owner-interface listeners opened, and which failure is reported when both cannot be opened?

In what order are the service-API and owner-interface listeners opened? Rule 1 does not list either listener, although the first failed check determines the diagnostic and which listener is opened and then closed.
Which surface's listener is opened and checked first?

quotes: The checks run in one order and the first that fails stops the start: no unknown item, taken in the order of their names by Unicode code point; the service tokens all four or none — none makes an owner-only start, and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; each secret's length (rule 3); their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule 5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the listener of each surface opened at the address the release fixes — the configuration names none (rule 1) — one that cannot be opened failing the start and closing those already opened.
Within one check, items go in the order rule 1 lists them.
judgement.divergence: One implementation opens the service-API listener first and reports it; another opens the owner-interface listener first and reports that one, which the owner notices in the startup diagnostic.
judgement.why: The texts require an ordered first-failure diagnostic but do not order the two listeners.

witness.initial: Every earlier startup check passes, and neither release-fixed listener can be opened.
outcomes: Startup stops with a diagnostic naming the service-API listener.
Startup stops with a diagnostic naming the owner-interface listener.
witness.observer: The owner reading the startup diagnostic.
basis: The checks run in one order and the first that fails stops the start: no unknown item, taken in the order of their names by Unicode code point; the service tokens all four or none — none makes an owner-only start, and some but not all fail on the first missing one in rule 1's order; every other item of rule 1 present; each well formed; each secret's length (rule 3); their distinctness (rule 4); the store and backup location apart (rule 5); the backup location writable, by a probe file under the temporary prefix (A18 rule 5); the store opening, or made new (rule 5); last, the listener of each surface opened at the address the release fixes — the configuration names none (rule 1) — one that cannot be opened failing the start and closing those already opened.

topics.topic: Required store state when rollback deletion fails after listener-opening failure
questions: What is the required outcome when listener opening fails and Registry cannot remove the store it just created?

When listener opening fails and deletion of the newly created store also fails, must startup preserve the empty store as the normative rule permits, or must it satisfy the test's unconditional no-store result by some other means?
Is leaving the empty new store permitted when cleanup cannot remove it, or must startup guarantee that no store remains after every listener-opening failure?

quotes: A failed start leaves no file it made but one it could not remove: a probe, which the next backup run removes with the other temporary files (A18 rule 4); a file of the store's temporary name, which the next start removes first (rule 5); or a store it made new for a start a listener then failed, which it removes — one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.

A start whose store is made new and whose listener then cannot be opened stops, serves nothing and leaves no store; one whose listener cannot be opened over an existing store leaves that store as it was.
judgement.divergence: The normative rule permits the undeletable empty store to remain, while required test 5 requires no store to remain; the owner and the next start observe the difference.
judgement.why: The required test states an unconditional no-store outcome that conflicts with the rule's explicit failed-removal exception.

bases.passage: A failed start leaves no file it made but one it could not remove: a probe, which the next backup run removes with the other temporary files (A18 rule 4); a file of the store's temporary name, which the next start removes first (rule 5); or a store it made new for a start a listener then failed, which it removes — one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.

A start whose store is made new and whose listener then cannot be opened stops, serves nothing and leaves no store; one whose listener cannot be opened over an existing store leaves that store as it was.

A start whose store is made new and whose listener then cannot be opened stops, serves nothing and leaves no store; one whose listener cannot be opened over an existing store leaves that store as it was.

witness.initial: The configured store is absent; Registry can create it, but a listener cannot be opened and the filesystem then refuses removal of the new store.
events: Registry creates the empty release-version store.
Registry fails to open a listener.
Registry attempts and fails to remove the new store.
outcomes: The empty store remains and the next start opens it as any store.
No store remains after the failed start.
witness.observer: The owner inspecting the store path and the next Registry start.
basis: the listener of each surface opened at the address the release fixes — the configuration names none (rule 1) — one that cannot be opened failing the start and closing those already opened.

topics.topic: Whether an owner-only start opens the service-API listener
questions: Must an owner-only start open the service-API listener, and must failure to open that unused listener stop the owner-only start?
In an owner-only start, is the service-API listener opened so Registry can refuse service calls, or is that listener absent because only the owner interface is served?

When all four service tokens are absent, is the service-API listener opened so that calls receive an authentication or authorization refusal, or is that listener absent so connection attempts fail at the network boundary?

quotes:
In an owner-only start the service API's listener is opened too
   and serves no operation: every service call is answered with a refusal at
   stage (1), whatever token it carries (A17 rule 1, "refuses every service
   call").
judgement.why: The State 4 start flow expressly opens the service-API listener in owner-only mode and refuses every service operation.

topics.topic: Concurrency protection and ownership proof before rollback removes a new store
questions: How is cleanup prevented from unlinking a newly created store that another concurrent Registry start has already opened?
Are concurrent starts excluded or locked, and if not, how does a failed start prove that the path still denotes its own untouched new store before removing it?

quotes: a store it made new for a start a listener then failed, which it removes — one it cannot remove is an empty store of the release's version, which the next start opens as any store.
judgement.why: The texts provide no basis establishing that two Registry starts may concurrently adopt the same configured store, so the proposed race cannot be made an admissible witness.

topics.topic: Scope and reference updates of the security re-review after A17 changes
questions: Did the re-review consider categories newly implicated by A17's new content, or only categories whose old reference lists already named A17; and should A17 now be referenced by `concurrency` and/or `files_artifacts`?

Were categories that did not previously name A17 also checked to determine whether A17's new listener acquisition, rollback deletion and concurrent-start behavior newly make A17 relevant, or were only categories already referencing A17 reviewed?

quotes: this review is complete for that catalogue and claims nothing beyond it.
A change to a decision a category names reopens this review.

Performed again on 2026-11-01, after that day's changes to A01, A04, A13, A16
and A17 reopened it (rule 2): every category naming them was reviewed, and no
outcome and no reference changed.
judgement.why: The texts do not disclose the re-review evidence, and the proposed newly implicated categories depend on the unwitnessed premise that concurrent starts against one store are admissible.

topics.topic: Behavior when a listener fails after successful startup
questions: If either surface's listener fails after a successful start, does Registry terminate and close the other surface, continue serving the other surface, or retry the failed listener?

quotes: last, the listener of each surface opened at the address the release fixes — the configuration names none (rule 1) — one that cannot be opened failing the start and closing those already opened.
judgement.why: Failure handling after startup is running-instance flow and operational lifecycle behaviour owned by State 4, not a State 2 startup check.

topics.topic: Diagnostics required when cleanup cannot remove a newly created store
questions: When listener opening fails and removal of the newly created store also fails, what diagnostic or diagnostics must Registry emit?

quotes:
A stopped start: one diagnostic naming the first failed item and no value,
  nothing served, no file left that the start made but one it could not
  remove — a probe, a file of the store's temporary name, or an empty store
  made new (A17 rule 2).
judgement.why: The State 4 start flow requires one diagnostic naming the first failed item, so the listener failure is diagnosed and the cleanup failure does not add a second diagnostic.
